0d6ddeeb0430.goldenSql: SELECT p.name AS postcode, COALESCE(a.name,'') AS place FROM locations p LEFT JOIN locations a ON a.id = p.areaid WHERE p.type='Postcode' AND p.lat BETWEEN ?-0.1 AND ?+0.1 AND p.lng BETWEEN ?-0.15 AND ?+0.15 ORDER BY ST_Distance_Sphere(POINT(p.lng,p.lat), POINT(?,?)) LIMIT 1
0d6ddeeb0430.reason: Nearest-postcode reverse-geocode lookup ordered by MySQL's ST_Distance_Sphere; a rewrite bug here would silently return the wrong place name for a given point.
0d6ddeeb0430.porting: MySQL POINT(lng,lat) -> PostGIS ST_MakePoint(lng,lat) (or ST_Point). MySQL ST_Distance_Sphere(geomA, geomB) -> PostGIS ST_DistanceSphere(geomA, geomB) - same semantics, great-circle distance in metres on a spherical-earth model, same two-geometry-argument signature. The BETWEEN bounding-box prefilter is unchanged, ANSI SQL.

13896214f40e.reason: Same tool, same batch loop and same runtime-built IN-list shape as q2 above (q3), fetching repliers for the sampled posts.
13896214f40e.porting: MySQL DATE_FORMAT(x, '%Y-%m-%d %H:%i:%s') -> PostgreSQL TO_CHAR(x, 'YYYY-MM-DD HH24:MI:SS'). Same IN (?,?,...) -> = ANY($1) array-parameter note as q2 above applies here too.

21a924629184.goldenSql: SELECT msgid, ST_X(point) AS lng, ST_Y(point) AS lat, msgtype, arrival, successful, promised, COALESCE(groupid, 0) FROM messages_spatial WHERE arrival BETWEEN ? AND ? AND msgtype IN ('Offer','Wanted') AND ST_Contains(ST_GeomFromText(?, 3857), point) ORDER BY arrival DESC LIMIT ?
21a924629184.reason: Spatial containment query against messages_spatial; core to member-area post retrieval, high blast radius if silently wrong.
21a924629184.porting: PostGIS: ST_Contains(geomA, geomB) and ST_GeomFromText(wkt, srid) are the identical function names and signatures; SRID 3857 (Web Mercator) is supported identically. ST_X/ST_Y are unchanged. No other MySQL-only syntax.

2c4fbf341113.goldenSql: SELECT id, nameshort, ST_AsGeoJSON(polyindex) FROM `groups` WHERE ST_Contains(polyindex, ST_GeomFromText(?, 3857)) LIMIT 8
2c4fbf341113.reason: Simulator-only endpoint, but shares the same `groups` spatial-containment shape as the live nearby-groups queries in groups.go; kept-raw for consistency with those rather than converted in isolation.
2c4fbf341113.porting: PostGIS: ST_AsGeoJSON, ST_Contains, ST_GeomFromText are identical function names and signatures. Backtick-quoted `groups` -> unquoted or double-quoted "groups" (not a Postgres reserved word).

4c807f7699ac.reason: Same tool as q1 above; fetches post metadata in batches of up to 500 ids (q2), with the IN-list built at runtime via strings.Join over one `?` placeholder per id - a genuine variable-arm builder, the same shape that repeatedly stayed raw during iznik-server-go's own conversion (plan 7.5) because the placeholder count is not fixed at compile time.
4c807f7699ac.porting: MySQL DATE_FORMAT(x, '%Y-%m-%d %H:%i:%s') -> PostgreSQL TO_CHAR(x, 'YYYY-MM-DD HH24:MI:SS'). MySQL IFNULL(x, y) -> PostgreSQL COALESCE(x, y). REPLACE(l.name, ' ', '') is ANSI-portable and unchanged. The hand-built IN (?,?,...) placeholder list should become a single = ANY($1) parameter bound to a Postgres array (pgx/lib/pq both support this) rather than porting the string concatenation as-is.

4d3e7b2533da.goldenSql: SELECT id, nameshort, ST_AsText(polyindex) AS wkt, ST_Contains(polyindex, ST_GeomFromText(CONCAT('POINT(', ?, ' ', ?, ')'), 3857)) AS contains_pt FROM `groups` WHERE publish = 1 AND listable = 1 AND polyindex IS NOT NULL AND ( ST_Contains(polyindex, ST_GeomFromText(CONCAT('POINT(', ?, ' ', ?, ')'), 3857)) OR ( ST_X(ST_Centroid(polyindex)) BETWEEN ? AND ? AND ST_Y(ST_Centroid(polyindex)) BETWEEN ? AND ? ) ) ORDER BY contains_pt DESC, ST_Distance(polyindex, ST_GeomFromText(CONCAT('POINT(', ?, ' ', ?, ')'), 3857)) ASC LIMIT 60
4d3e7b2533da.reason: The core nearby-groups query: a spatial containment test plus a centroid-distance fallback and an ORDER BY combining both; a rewrite bug here would silently reorder or drop groups a member should see.
4d3e7b2533da.porting: PostGIS: ST_Contains, ST_GeomFromText, ST_Centroid, ST_Distance, ST_X/ST_Y are all identical function names and signatures. MySQL CONCAT('POINT(', ?, ' ', ?, ')') -> PostgreSQL CONCAT(...) works identically (Postgres's CONCAT has been variadic since 9.1), or better, switch to ST_MakePoint(?, ?) directly and drop the WKT string-building entirely. Backtick-quoted `groups` -> unquoted/double-quoted.

4fac5300351b.goldenSql: SELECT ms.msgid, ST_X(ms.point) AS lng, ST_Y(ms.point) AS lat, ms.msgtype, ms.arrival, ms.successful, ms.promised, COALESCE(ms.groupid, 0) AS groupid, COALESCE(g.nameshort, '') AS groupname, COALESCE(m.fromuser, 0) AS fromuser, COALESCE(m.subject, '') AS subject, (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(ml.count), 0) FROM messages_likes ml WHERE ml.msgid = ms.msgid AND ml.type = 'View') AS views, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM chat_messages cm WHERE cm.refmsgid = ms.msgid AND cm.type = 'Interested' AND cm.reviewrejected = 0 AND cm.reviewrequired = 0) AS replies, COALESCE( (SELECT a.id FROM messages_attachments a WHERE a.msgid = ms.msgid ORDER BY a.`primary` DESC, a.id ASC LIMIT 1), 0) AS thumb_attachment_id, COALESCE( (SELECT a.externaluid FROM messages_attachments a WHERE a.msgid = ms.msgid AND a.externaluid IS NOT NULL ORDER BY a.`primary` DESC, a.id ASC LIMIT 1), '') AS thumb_externaluid, EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM messages_outcomes mo WHERE mo.msgid = ms.msgid) AS has_outcome, EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM messages_outcomes mo WHERE mo.msgid = ms.msgid AND mo.outcome IN ('Taken','Received')) AS has_success, COALESCE(m.tnpostid, 0) AS tnpostid, COALESCE(m.locationid, 0) AS locationid, COALESCE(m.textbody, '') AS textbody FROM messages_spatial ms LEFT JOIN messages m ON m.id = ms.msgid LEFT JOIN `groups` g ON g.id = ms.groupid WHERE ms.arrival >= ? AND ms.msgtype IN ('Offer','Wanted') AND ST_Contains(ST_GeomFromText(?, 3857), ms.point) ORDER BY ms.arrival DESC LIMIT ?
4fac5300351b.reason: Large multi-join simulator query mixing spatial containment with several correlated subqueries (view/reply counts, thumbnail attachment, outcome flags); genuinely hard to express as a single mechanical ORM chain without materially changing its shape - the kind of site plan 7.5 describes.
4fac5300351b.porting: PostGIS: ST_X/ST_Y/ST_Contains/ST_GeomFromText are unchanged. Backtick-quoted identifiers (`groups`, the a.`primary` column alias) -> double-quoted ("groups", a."primary"). The EXISTS/correlated-subquery structure is unchanged, ANSI SQL.

6d34bf440462.reason: Offline batch data-extraction tool for the ripple simulator (not the HTTP service, but still queries the live Percona cluster directly); enumerates candidate post IDs via a correlated EXISTS subquery (q1). The SQL text is static - only the one bind value (cutoff date) varies - so despite being read from a `q1` variable rather than a string literal, there is no dynamic query-shape risk in this particular statement.
6d34bf440462.porting: No change required for PostgreSQL: ANSI INNER JOIN/EXISTS/IN, no MySQL-only syntax.

c6c51faba676.goldenSql: SELECT STRAIGHT_JOIN DISTINCT m.groupid, COALESCE(pl.lat, ual.lat), COALESCE(pl.lng, ual.lng) FROM users_approxlocs ual INNER JOIN memberships m ON m.userid = ual.userid AND m.collection = 'Approved' INNER JOIN users u ON u.id = ual.userid AND u.lastaccess >= NOW() - INTERVAL 90 DAY INNER JOIN `groups` g ON g.id = m.groupid AND g.publish = 1 AND g.listable = 1 AND ST_GeometryType(g.polyindex) IN ('POLYGON', 'MULTIPOLYGON') LEFT JOIN locations pl ON pl.id = u.lastlocation AND pl.type = 'Postcode' AND NOT (pl.lat = 0 AND pl.lng = 0) WHERE MBRContains(ST_GeomFromText(?, 3857), ual.position) AND ST_Contains(g.polyindex, ST_SRID(POINT(COALESCE(pl.lng, ual.lng), COALESCE(pl.lat, ual.lat)), 3857))
c6c51faba676.reason: The most MySQL-specific statement in this service: a STRAIGHT_JOIN optimizer hint plus an MBRContains bounding-box prefilter and an exact ST_Contains check combined. The join-order hint has no direct Postgres equivalent, so this needs a human decision at Phase 4, not a mechanical rewrite.
c6c51faba676.porting: STRAIGHT_JOIN has no PostgreSQL equivalent - Postgres's planner does not take join-order hints without the third-party pg_hint_plan extension; drop the hint, rely on Postgres's planner and appropriate indexes, and re-check the plan with EXPLAIN after porting. MBRContains(bbox, geom) -> PostGIS: the `&&` bounding-box overlap operator against a GiST index, or ST_Intersects for an exact equivalent. ST_Contains/ST_GeomFromText/ST_SRID are unchanged. POINT(lng,lat) -> ST_MakePoint(lng,lat). NOW() - INTERVAL 90 DAY -> NOW() - INTERVAL '90 days'. Backtick-quoted `groups` -> unquoted/double-quoted.
